coordinates.origin: Identity root at footprint center; lowest contact Z=0. Units are meters.

concept.reason: Preparation inspected the actual holotype CT thumbnail and the scale-bearing skeletal reconstruction. Maker re-inspected both private images before original geometry construction. No generated concept was needed or used.

scope: Complete small early mammal with compact trunk and robust scratch-digging forelimbs; not isolated claws or skeleton.

scale.status: The approximately 16 cm total length comes from Scott Hartman's author reconstruction with a 2 cm scale. Head-body, tail and height targets are approximate silhouette-derived design dimensions, not measurements of a complete fossil.

diagnostic_targets: Low compact mammaliaform trunk with a relatively small elongated wedge muzzle and slender tapering tail, not a bushy squirrel tail.
Very robust proximal forelimbs and broad shoulders; shortened sturdy hands bearing broad flattened digging claws. Forelimbs visibly stronger than the hindlegs.
Five manual digits in a conservative mammalian restoration. Central digging fingers prominent; flattened spoon-like claws with single tips, not bifid hooks, needle cones or oversized scythe blades.
Low stance with forelimbs angled outward and downward as a scratch-digger, not fully subterranean mole paddles. Hindfeet elongated, flatter and planted.
Long gently tapering slender tail; no armor plates, webbing or echidna spines.
Separate small eyes and understated ears. Short coherent coat with no invented stripe pattern; surface detail is secondary to digging-forelimb silhouette.
uncertainties: LACM 150948 comprises jaws, incomplete cranium and about 40 percent of the postcranial skeleton. It is not a complete preserved skeleton.
Full outline, ears, fur, tail completion and coloration are reconstructed; they must not be presented as preserved soft tissue.
Basal mammalian placement is not resolved here. Do not label this animal an armadillo, anteater or confirmed placental.
Scratch-digging and specialized feeding interpretations are supported by limb and tooth anatomy; exact diet remains interpretive. No detailed exposed dentition is required.
Total length of approximately 16 cm is a published skeletal reconstruction estimate, not a measured holotype body length.
acceptance_checklist: Forearm and hand substantially more robust than hindleg, with broad flattened claws and plausible attachments.
Low compact trunk, slender tapering tail and wedge head distinguish the restoration from an ordinary mouse or squirrel.
Four exact-GLB front, side, top and perspective views; separated digging claws visible in top and perspective.
Self-contained source/deps; two deterministic isolated rebuilds; independent QA remains separate.

surface_profile.palette_note: Neutral brown coat and pale claws are conjectural, not preserved colors.
